classification.difficultyReason: Convert the given angle from west to its complement from north, interpret the reverse direction using the parallel compass axes, and express both directions as compass and true bearings.

content.prompt: Express each of the following as a compass bearing and a true bearing.

spec.description: P is northwest of Q, joined by a solid segment. Each endpoint has dashed compass axes and a north arrow. At Q the angle from QP to west is 40 degrees.
spec.mathematics: Q-P is proportional to (sin130, cos130); QP lies 40 degrees north of west.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 40-degree angle is labelled; neither requested bearing is supplied.

answer.worked:
The line is $40^\circ$ from the east–west direction, so it is $50^\circ$ from the north–south direction.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Angle east of south}&=90^\circ-40^\circ\\\text{Angle east of south}&=50^\circ\\\text{True bearing}&=180^\circ-50^\circ\\\text{True bearing}&=130^\circ\mathrm{T}.\end{align*}$$
The compass bearing is $\mathrm{S}50^\circ\mathrm{E}$.

$QP$ is $40^\circ$ north of west.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Angle west of north}&=90^\circ-40^\circ\\\text{Angle west of north}&=50^\circ\\\text{True bearing}&=360^\circ-50^\circ\\\text{True bearing}&=310^\circ\mathrm{T}.\end{align*}$$
The compass bearing is $\mathrm{N}50^\circ\mathrm{W}$.
